speaker: Doctor
text: That will help narrow things down. To better understand the progression, have you noticed any fluid leaking from these red bumps or any change in their color? Also, do you recall any recent travel, insect exposure, or new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies infestation. The combination of intense pruritus, new-onset red bumps, and recent travel to a high-density conference setting is highly suggestive of scabies, particularly given the lateral spread from the thigh. I recommend a skin scraping for microscopy to confirm the presence of mites and eggs.
